question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Here are 5 ideas that were proposed for this question:

1. Barcoded lineage tracing across a state transition: Use clonal DNA barcodes to split sister cells, measuring AP-1 motif accessibility or FOS/JUN levels in one half and challenging the other half with a stimulus such as a drug or differentiation cue. Ask whether the pre-measured AP-1 state predicts the clone's eventual fate, the core test of a heritable, predictive memory.
2. Degron-based timed removal separating establishment from maintenance: Tag c-JUN/c-FOS with an auxin or dTAG degron (or express dominant-negative A-FOS) and deplete AP-1 either during a priming stimulus or only after it ends. Memory requires that post-stimulus depletion erases the primed response even though the initiating signal is already gone.
3. Direct measurement of persistence and heritability timescales: Track an endogenous AP-1 reporter such as a knock-in FOS-HaloTag or AP-1 motif-driven fluorophore by live imaging across many divisions. Extract state autocorrelation times, mother-daughter correlations, and switching rates to distinguish true multigenerational memory from slow protein turnover.
4. Decoupling AP-1 binding from chromatin accessibility: Perform paired ATAC-seq and CUT&RUN for JUN/FOS before, during, and long after stimulation to test whether stimulus-opened enhancers remain accessible after AP-1 unbinds. This asks whether AP-1 acts as a pioneer factor that writes a latent chromatin memory read out upon restimulation.
5. Synthetic write/erase perturbation of specific AP-1 enhancers: Use dCas9-VPR or targeted recruitment of JUN to a defined set of AP-1-bound enhancers, plus CRISPRi or deletion to remove them. Test whether transiently imposing the AP-1 state suffices to install a long-lived primed phenotype and whether erasing those elements abolishes memory of prior exposure.

A senior expert reviewing them says they are the ideas everyone in the field would propose first. Propose 5 replacement ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that are substantially less obvious but still concrete, scientifically sound, and feasible for a research lab. Do not repeat or lightly modify the ideas above. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Heterokaryon fusion test of cis- versus trans-encoded memory
ideas.description: Fuse stimulus-primed cells with naive cells (distinguished by nuclear-localized fluorophores or species-specific reads) and assay, nucleus-by-nucleus, whether primed AP-1 target expression and accessibility spread to the naive nucleus or stay confined to the primed one. Trans-dominant transfer implicates a diffusible AP-1 protein/dimer pool as the store, whereas strictly nucleus-autonomous persistence implicates chromatin-encoded memory at AP-1 sites, a distinction that bulk time courses cannot make.

ideas.title: Allele-specific memory at heterozygous AP-1 motifs
ideas.description: In F1 hybrid cells (or CRISPR-generated heterozygotes in which the TRE/CRE motif is destroyed on one allele only), use allele-resolved ATAC, CUT&RUN, and nascent RNA to ask whether primed accessibility and faster re-induction persist exclusively on the motif-bearing allele within the same nucleus. Because both alleles share one cytoplasm and one trans environment, allele discordance is a near-airtight demonstration that the memory is written in cis at AP-1 elements rather than inherited as a cellular signaling state.

ideas.title: Open-loop feedback clamp on AP-1 autoregulation
ideas.description: Replace the endogenous AP-1 binding sites in the JUN/FOS/FOSL1 regulatory regions with an orthogonal doxycycline- or rapamycin-controlled input, titrating dose so that mean and cell-to-cell variance of AP-1 protein match wild type under acute stimulation. If memory collapses in these open-loop cells despite matched acute responses, the memory resides in transcriptional positive feedback; if it survives, feedback is dispensable and a chromatin or cofactor mechanism must carry it.

ideas.title: Binding kinetics and single-fiber co-occupancy as the remembered variable
ideas.description: Compare naive and long-after-stimulus primed cells by single-molecule tracking of HaloTagged JUN (residence times, bound fraction, search time, cluster/condensate formation) and by single-molecule methyltransferase footprinting (Fiber-seq/SAMOSA) that reports actual protein occupancy and combinatorial co-accessibility of linked enhancers on the same DNA fiber. This tests whether memory is stored as altered AP-1 binding kinetics or as coordinated multi-enhancer configurations, rather than as changes in AP-1 abundance or bulk accessibility.

ideas.title: Information-theoretic bottleneck test with designed stimulus histories
ideas.description: Expose single cells to a library of distinguishable stimulus histories (varying order, spacing, amplitude), then jointly measure AP-1 state and downstream phenotype in the same cells and compute mutual information between history and AP-1 state, history and phenotype, and the conditional information remaining once AP-1 state is known. If AP-1 is the memory channel, the data-processing inequality should hold with little history information bypassing it; substantial residual information identifies a parallel, non-AP-1 memory store and bounds how much of the memory AP-1 can possibly explain.
